I'm sketching a Penrose-style serpent: a body shaped like an impossible tribar, with its head at one corner biting its own tail. I'm also considering tiny legs on each beam, placed in impossible orientations in the spirit of Escher, and I'm working out the triangle's geometry from a standard construction.

Still checking how the trapezoid's edges overlap the neighbouring piece along the right side, and tightening the bottom stripe so it stops short of that corner.

Still working out the piece boundaries: I'm settling on a trapezoid for the bottom stripe, with its top edge running across the inner strip, and checking that the lengths of its parallel sides add up.

Still working out how the outer stripe and the inner stripe fit together on the left side, checking whether the notch at the corner can be avoided.

Still working out the L-shaped piece's corners, testing a version where the cap belongs to one stripe and the other stripes follow by rotation.

Now I'm settling the coordinates of the tribar's three pieces and converting them to screen pixels. I'm considering turning the shape into an animal, perhaps a snake or lizard with the impossible triangle as its body, and possibly adding a head and tail.

I'm weighing whether to add legs along the beams, maybe small ones on the outer faces and a few pointing into the hole, but that might suggest the wrong side is down. I'm leaning toward keeping the creature simple and letting the head and tail do the work.

I'm deciding how the head and tail should attach to the impossible triangle, weighing whether to keep the loop closed like an ouroboros or open it so the head and tail come out from two corners.

I'm picturing the head as an oval sitting over the bottom-left corner, with its snout pointing down toward the start of the bottom bar, so the serpent seems to bite the body it's made from.

I'm picturing the head coming down the left side and stopping just short of the bottom corner, with its jaws open around the start of the bottom bar, as though the serpent is trying to bite its own tail where the piece's edge begins.

I'm weighing where the head should go: the top corner is roomier than the bottom-left, so I'm considering the head extending up and to the left from the top cap, where there's space on the canvas.

razonamiento:
Voy a responder con honestidad, en español rioplatense y en primera persona, en menos de 200 palabras. Lo que hice fue una serpiente cuyo cuerpo es un triángulo de Penrose: tres barras que parecen pasar cada una por delante de la siguiente, una figura imposible, con las escamas rotadas 120° en cada barra.

Ahora me doy cuenta de que no tengo acceso a cómo llegué a esa decisión, así que solo puedo inferirla a partir del SVG y debo decirlo con honestidad.
